name: woocommerce
title: WooCommerce
description: Cart, checkout and order events from WooCommerce's own storefront DOM events, plus order data printed on the order-received page.

platforms.name: WooCommerce
platforms.notes: Cart and Checkout blocks. Classic themes are covered through the jQuery added_to_cart event.

journey.label: Adds socks on a classic theme
journey.fixture: added to cart on a classic theme

howItWorks.summary: Listens for the DOM events WooCommerce's Cart and Checkout blocks already dispatch, and reads the order the companion WordPress plugin prints on the order-received page. Nothing is added to your theme.

steps.title: Reads the store, the customer and the order
steps.detail: At init it reads `window.ddRumWooCommerce`, which the companion WordPress plugin prints: store and customer on every page, plus the order on the order-received page. The store becomes session context, the WordPress user ID goes to `setUser`, and the order becomes `commerce.purchase`.

steps.title: Listens on document.body
steps.detail: It adds one native listener per WooCommerce event on `document.body`: `wc-blocks_added_to_cart`, `wc-blocks_removed_from_cart` and `wc-blocks_product_list_rendered` from the blocks, plus `added_to_cart` and `removed_from_cart` for classic themes. Each event carries the Store API cart in `detail.cart`, which the plugin maps to the commerce schema.

steps.title: Classic themes and jQuery
steps.detail: `window.jQuery` is in the footprint because classic themes raise `added_to_cart` through it. The plugin listens with native `addEventListener` only, so it sees the event when a theme dispatches it as a DOM event, and not when a theme fires it only through jQuery.

steps.title: Reports the checkout funnel on request
steps.detail: Cart views, checkout, shipping, payment and search have no WooCommerce DOM event. The WordPress plugin, or a theme, reports them by calling `createCheckoutReporter` from the blocks' hooks (`window.DD_RUM_PLUGINS.woocommerce.createCheckoutReporter` on the CDN).

steps.title: Counts each order once
steps.detail: The core records each sent `transaction_id` in `dd_rum_commerce_seen` in localStorage for 24 hours, so a reloaded order-received page does not send the purchase again.
